question: Ari has searched their library this turn with [Bog Glider]. During their end step, Nico casts [Mission Briefing]. Can they use it to cast [Archive Trap] from their graveyard for free?
answer:
Yes — Nico can cast Archive Trap from their graveyard for {0}.

How it works, step by step:

1. Mission Briefing resolves: Nico surveils 2 and chooses an instant or sorcery card in their graveyard — Archive Trap. Mission Briefing grants permission to cast Archive Trap this turn (and replaces putting it into the graveyard with exile). Mission Briefing does not change *when* Archive Trap can be cast [Mission Briefing ruling #4]; since Archive Trap is an instant, casting it during an end step with priority is fine. It also doesn't change what Archive Trap costs.

2. Archive Trap's own text says "If an opponent searched their library this turn, you may pay {0} rather than pay this spell's mana cost." That's an alternative cost (a cost paid instead of the mana cost, per 118.9/118.9a), and an object's ability that lets a player pay an alternative cost functions on the stack while the spell is being cast [113.6d] — so it works no matter which zone Archive Trap is cast from, including the graveyard via Mission Briefing.

3. Bog Glider's activated ability reads "Search your library for a Mercenary permanent card...", so Ari genuinely searched their library [Archive Trap ruling #1], and it doesn't matter whether Ari actually found and took a card [Archive Trap ruling #2, Bog Glider ruling #1]. Since Ari is Nico's opponent and the search happened this turn, Archive Trap's condition is met.

4. Nico announces the intent to pay the {0} alternative cost as part of casting Archive Trap [601.2b]. Only one alternative cost may be applied to a spell [118.9a, 601.2b]; Mission Briefing merely grants permission to cast from the graveyard and imposes no cost of its own, so nothing conflicts here. Archive Trap's mana cost and mana value remain {3}{U}{U} and 5 — only the amount actually paid changes [Archive Trap ruling #4].

Assumption on timing: I'm reading "their end step" as the end step of the turn in which Ari searched, i.e., the same turn. Both Mission Briefing's "you may cast it this turn" and Archive Trap's "searched their library this turn" are satisfied only within that same turn, so Nico must actually cast Archive Trap before the turn ends. If the search had happened on an earlier turn, Archive Trap could still be cast off Mission Briefing but only for its full {3}{U}{U} mana cost.

Multiplayer note: Archive Trap only asks whether *an* opponent searched, so at a table with more than two players any opponent of Nico's searching turns it on, and the opponent Nico targets to mill thirteen doesn't have to be Ari [Archive Trap ruling #8]. With exactly two players, Ari is necessarily both the searcher and the only legal target.

Finally, when Archive Trap finishes resolving it will be exiled instead of going to the graveyard, because it was cast via Mission Briefing.

If the value of that variable is defined in the text of the spell by a choice that player would make later in the announcement or resolution of the spell, that player makes that choice at this time instead of that later time. If a cost that will be paid as the spell is being cast includes Phyrexian mana symbols, the player announces whether they intend to pay 2 life or a corresponding colored mana cost for each of those symbols. Previously made choices (such as choosing to cast a spell with flashback from a graveyard or choosing to cast a creature with morph face down) may restrict the player’s options when making these choices.

question: In a game of Two-Headed Giant, Antonio activates the last loyalty ability of [Chandra, Hope's Beacon] with X=1. Could they target both Nico and Noah?
answer:
Yes. Chandra, Hope's Beacon's last ability reads "−X: Chandra deals X damage to each of up to two targets," so with X=1 Antonio may choose two different targets — Nico and Noah — and Chandra, Hope's Beacon deals 1 damage to each of them. "Up to two targets" means two *separate* targets, so both players can be chosen; you just can't choose the same player twice.

How the damage is applied in Two-Headed Giant: damage happens to each player individually, and the result is applied to that player's team's shared life total [810.9]. So if Nico and Noah are on the same team, that team's shared life total drops by 2 total (1 from Nico, 1 from Noah). If Nico and Noah are on different teams, each team's shared life total drops by 1. Life totals are one of the few shared resources in Two-Headed Giant [810.5], [810.9].

Two side notes:
- The cost is −1 (X=1), so Chandra, Hope's Beacon goes from 5 loyalty to 4 if it was at 5.
- Chandra, Hope's Beacon's copy ability ("Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, copy it") does not apply here — a loyalty ability is an activated ability, not a cast instant or sorcery spell, so nothing gets copied and the damage isn't doubled.

This answer is specific to Two-Headed Giant [810.1]; in an ordinary two-player game the same ability could likewise hit two targets, but there'd be no shared life total to apply the damage to.
